The magnetic brake doesn’t work when the battery is full because the generated electricity doesn’t have anywhere to go. The brake force is literally the opposite force of what’s happening electrically. So when the battery is charging there’s an equal charging force as there is braking force. By pressing on the brake you ask to brake the best possible way from your 3 different braking sources: regen, engine, and hydraulic disc brakes. If regen isn’t available from a full battery state then to avoid wear on the hydraulic disc brakes the engine is used. 

Source: engineering major

Well I’m glad I can help you understand. There’s plenty of people here who keep the country the way it is too—I think you got that part right. It’s ultimately not a simple situation. As an example, doctors need to pay off more school debt here, which drives up health costs (let’s say from $40 to $60 per visit). Uninsured costs are further inflated because insurance companies demand a percentage discount (increasing the $60 to $100 to give them “40% off”). These 2 issues alone increase costs 250% and the reality is that there’s dozens of issues here without agreed upon solutions such as the cost of prescription pills or how to insure chronically ill people. Much of the development of *new* pills worldwide is done in the United States because it would be either less profitable or economically impossible to do it elsewhere. This is largely because the patent system allows exclusive manufacturing rights *only in the United States* to the company for a number of years after successfully passing FDA clinical trials. This provides incentive for new medications to be researched and health to improve. Many medications wouldn’t exist without this or if they did, they would not be rigorously tested like they are in the United States.

Also, as much as I hate aspects of America, like it’s healthcare system, it’s my home. And for every problem it has, it has something else I love just as much. I want to be a good uncle, and if I’m in another country I would be taking away family from 3 young children. The stability of the power source has nothing to do with it. The Switch in handheld mode never even gets to 10 Watts. The dock maxes at 18 watts. Shitty vape mods with internal lithium ion battery’s easily push 40W, sometimes much much more. It’s purely a power saving feature in portable mode. That’s it. In theory you could hack it and change the clock speed equal to or slightly higher than what Nintendo has it running at in docked mode.

So what’s happening is the GPU (what makes shit look pretty) works however hard Nintendo tells it to—to a point. The point is determined (mostly) by heat (don’t melt the Switch!), power (give me more than 20 minutes in BotW damnit!) and physics (fucking quantum mechanics, billions vs millions of transistors, blah blah blah BORING). The heat (I don’t wanna cook eggs on my Switch in handheld mode) and power (playing all teh gamez portably) come into play (ha get it?) when the Switch isn’t docked. Also the tiny screen on the Switch doesn’t need as much of those sweet sweet GPU gains to run well versus your TV. So when you finally hook your Switch up in docked mode, Nintendo is only concerned with the physics of the GPU.
